A reference at the end or a private evidence caveat does not make this a descriptive summary of the authors’ view.

issues.finding: The instruction about not putting a baby into positions they cannot yet reach themselves broadens a qualified discussion into an absolute rule. It can imply that ordinary lying on the tummy/back or being held must also wait for independent entry into those positions, and can make the depicted tummy position read as an achievement requirement. The original page specifically discusses propping into sitting/standing and separately describes lying on the back or stomach when not held.

issue.suggestedRevision: In descriptive prose, preserve the distinction rather than the broad prohibition: The authors distinguish lying on the back or tummy from propping a baby into sitting or standing before they can get there independently. Retain context that help is available; do not convert this suggested summary back into a positioning command. The source reviewer must review the exact revised wording and reference.
